answer: Zero-knowledge uniqueness proofs curb Sybil attacks by verifying membership in an accredited registry alongside a deterministic nullifier that blocks duplicate registrations per epoch without exposing the holder. Attackers incur the verifiable acquisition cost of securing a distinct credential per identity for agents routing tide telemetry or auditing yarrow harvests over a multi-year horizon. However, illicit credential rental markets can still supply colluding identities for a fee.
